🎙 Iran says lifting of oil sanctions discussed at Switzerland talks

📌 Burgenstock, IRNA – The managing director of the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC), Hamid Bovard, says that lifting oil sanctions and related exemptions was a topic of discussion during the quadrilateral talks in Switzerland.

In an interview on Sunday, Bovard, a member of Iran’s delegation at the quadrilateral negotiations in Switzerland, announced that the naval blockade has been lifted and Iran’s oil exports will resume through the Persian Gulf.
​
He added, “In the first phase, Iranian vessels have crossed the previously restricted imaginary line and are now heading toward their intended destinations.”
​
“In recent days, nearly half of the country’s monthly oil exports have been shipped abroad. With the full implementation of the memorandum, exports will continue at full capacity,” he noted.
​
Furthermore, Bovard said, “During the negotiations, we seriously pursued issues related to investment and the lifting of oil sanctions. Amendments have also been proposed to the American side regarding this matter, which we hope to implement.”
​
The Iranian delegation arrived at Zurich Airport at around 10 p.m. local time Saturday, led by Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who also heads the negotiating team.
​
Accompanying Ghalibaf were Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi; Ali Bagheri, the Deputy for International Affairs at the Supreme National Security Council Secretariat; Abdolnaser Hemmati, the Governor of the Central Bank of Iran; Hamid Bovard, the Deputy Oil Minister and CEO of the National Iranian Oil Company; Kazem Gharibabadi, the Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs; and Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei.
​
On the American side, US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner, advisor to US President Donald Trump, and US Vice President JD Vance were present in Switzerland to join the talks.
